title: idempotent-tenant-rbac-seed-and-rollback-support-for-private-installer
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require a reproducible, least-privilege bootstrap path that works for both cloud VPC and on-prem clusters and can survive installer upgrades and rollbacks. Current manual seeding leads to drift (duplicate RoleBindings, stale bootstrap secrets) and causes permission errors during automated upgrades. This PR introduces an idempotent tenant RBAC seeding flow that is safe to run multiple times and integrates with the installer Helm chart and Terraform modules used by the private deployment flow.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new Terraform module (modules/tenant-bootstrap) that performs server-side apply via kubectl provider to create Namespaces, Roles, ClusterRoles, and RoleBindings required for tenant isolation. The module exposes a single variable `bootstrap_token_kms_key` to ensure the bootstrap secret can be KMS-wrapped for air-gapped/on-prem HSM setups.
- Updates the private-installer Helm chart to include a pre-install and post-upgrade hook (`templates/hooks/tenant-seed-hook.yaml`) that calls the tenant-bootstrap job. Hooks are implemented as a Job that runs `rbac-seed` container image (small Go binary) which reconciles desired RBAC objects using server-side apply and ownerReferences to ensure idempotency. Hooks are marked with `helm.sh/hook-weight` and `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy` so failed installs can be retried cleanly.
- Adds a `rbac-seed` controller image and job manifest that supports a dry-run mode and emits structured logs for tracing in the Console. The binary checks for pre-existing objects and only creates or updates when necessary; it is tolerant of transient API errors and retries with backoff.
- Terraform test coverage: integration test workspace (tests/terraform/tenant-bootstrap) that runs `terraform apply` against a KinD cluster in CI, verifies RoleBindings, and asserts that re-applying the module is a no-op (no additional diffs).
- Rollback support: the Helm hook records a stable ConfigMap checksum and the seed job sets ownerReferences so that when a release is rolled back the old RBAC objects are retained only if still referenced. We also add a lightweight cleanup job (templates/cleanup-hook.yaml) that runs on `post-delete` for releases that opt-in via values.x.cleanupOnDelete = true.
- Security: bootstrap token secret is created as a Kubernetes Secret with annotations linking to the KMS key; secret is short-lived by default (72h) and a rotation job is optionally installed by the Terraform module for managed setups.

Why this is different from prior work: existing RBAC bootstrap PRs focused on static role templates. This change introduces an orchestrated, idempotent seeding flow wired into both Terraform and Helm, supports KMS-backed secrets for Private, and explicitly handles upgrade/rollback semantics so CI/topology changes don't cause permission regressions.

Files changed (high level):
- modules/tenant-bootstrap/main.tf (new) - Terraform module implementing server-side apply and secret creation
- helm/private-installer/templates/hooks/tenant-seed-hook.yaml (new) - pre-install/post-upgrade hook Job
- helm/private-installer/templates/hooks/cleanup-hook.yaml (new) - optional post-delete cleanup Job
- images/rbac-seed/main.go (new) - small reconciler binary with server-side apply logic
- images/rbac-seed/Dockerfile (new)
- tests/terraform/tenant-bootstrap/ (new integration test workspace)
- docs/private/rbac-bootstrap.md (new) - operator-facing doc and manual troubleshooting steps

Minimal illustrative snippet (from rbac-seed reconciliation logic):
`kubectl apply --server-side -f <generated-yaml> --field-manager=rbac-seed`

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests for the Go binary using fake clients and an integration Terraform test against KinD that runs in the `rbac-e2e` workflow.
- CI: initial runs showed intermittent KinD network flakiness (failing test `TestTerraformApply`) which we fixed by adding an exponential backoff and increasing KinD network readiness timeout. Current CI status: pass.

Upgrade plan / rollouts:
- Release the Terraform module as v0.1.0 in the private-installer chart repo.
- For existing customers we will ship a one-off runbook to create the bootstrap secret with their KMS key and run the terraform module in `plan` mode before applying.

Manual verification steps (for reviewers / SRE):
1) Deploy Helm chart with `values.rbac.enable=true` and `values.cleanupOnDelete=false` to a KinD cluster.
2) Confirm Job runs and exits 0, check the `rbac-seed` logs for `reconcile complete`.
3) Re-run `helm upgrade` (no changes) and assert that `rbac-seed` job is a no-op (log: `no changes`).
4) Inspect created Roles and RoleBindings to ensure they have the expected ownerReferences and KMS annotations on secrets.

Related: references ENG-2145 for the original design doc, SEC-108 for KMS secret pattern, and SUP-977 which was the support ticket motivating idempotent behavior during upgrades.

Checklist: 
- [x] Terraform module implemented and documented
- [x] Helm hooks added and tested
- [x] idempotent reconcile logic and ownerReferences implemented
- [x] CI integration test added and stabilized
- [x] Manual runbook and docs added

Notes: this change was kept conservative to avoid accidental privilege widening. The Terraform module requires an explicit `grant_admin` boolean to create any ClusterRoleBindings (default false). The `rbac-seed` binary runs as a low-privilege service account in the installer job and performs only the minimal operations defined in the module's outputs.

release_notes: Added an idempotent tenant RBAC bootstrap flow for Private installer: new Terraform module (tenant-bootstrap), Helm pre-install/post-upgrade hooks for seeding RBAC, optional cleanup on delete, KMS-backed bootstrap secret support, and integration tests. No automatic ClusterRoleBinding creation unless `grant_admin=true`.
